functions.name: apply
functions.summary: The `apply` function is a performance-optimized alternative to the native `Function#apply`, designed to invoke a specified function (`func`) with a given `this` context (`thisArg`) and an array of arguments (`args`). It efficiently handles up to three arguments directly, falling back to the native `apply` method for larger argument arrays, making it useful for scenarios where function invocation speed is critical.

functions.name: arrayAggregator
functions.summary: The `arrayAggregator` function iterates over an array, applying a provided `setter` function to accumulate values in an `accumulator` object, using a transformed key generated by the `iteratee` function for each element. This function is useful for custom aggregation of array elements into an object based on specific transformation and accumulation logic.

functions.name: arrayEach
functions.summary: The `arrayEach` function iterates over each element in a given array, invoking a specified callback function (`iteratee`) for each element. It stops the iteration if the callback returns `false`, making it useful for cases where early termination of the loop is needed based on a condition.

functions.name: arrayEachRight
functions.summary: The `arrayEachRight` function iterates over an array in reverse order, invoking a provided callback function (`iteratee`) for each element. It stops the iteration if the callback returns `false`, making it useful for scenarios where you need to process elements from the end of the array towards the beginning.

functions.name: arrayEvery
functions.summary: The `arrayEvery` function checks if all elements in a given array satisfy a specified predicate function, returning `true` if they do and `false` otherwise. It is useful for validating that every item in an array meets certain criteria without relying on shorthand syntax for the predicate.

functions.name: arrayFilter
functions.summary: The `arrayFilter` function iterates over an input array and applies a provided predicate function to each element, returning a new array that contains only the elements for which the predicate returns true. This function is useful for filtering arrays based on specific criteria without relying on shorthand syntax.

functions.name: arrayIncludes
functions.summary: The `arrayIncludes` function checks if a specified value is present in a given array, returning `true` if found and `false` otherwise. It is a specialized utility for quickly determining the existence of an element in an array without the need to specify a starting index for the search.

functions.name: arrayIncludesWith
functions.summary: The `arrayIncludesWith` function checks if a specified value exists in an array using a custom comparator function to determine equality. This is useful when standard equality checks are insufficient, allowing for more complex comparisons between elements.

functions.name: arrayMap
functions.summary: The `arrayMap` function takes an array and an iteratee function as inputs, applying the iteratee to each element of the array and returning a new array containing the results. It is a specialized implementation of the mapping operation, designed for scenarios where shorthand iteratee syntax is not supported.

functions.name: arrayPush
functions.summary: The `arrayPush` function appends the elements of the `values` array to the end of the `array`, modifying the original array in place. This function is useful for efficiently combining two arrays without creating a new one, making it ideal for scenarios where memory usage needs to be minimized.

functions.name: arrayReduce
functions.summary: The `arrayReduce` function iterates over an array, applying a specified `iteratee` function to accumulate a single result, starting from an optional initial value (`accumulator`). It is a specialized version of the `_.reduce` method tailored for arrays, allowing for more control over the accumulation process, especially when the initial value needs to be derived from the first element of the array.

functions.name: arrayReduceRight
functions.summary: The `arrayReduceRight` function iterates over an array from right to left, applying a specified `iteratee` function to each element and an accumulator, which can be initialized with the last element of the array if `initAccum` is true. This function is useful for reducing an array into a single value while processing elements in reverse order, which can be beneficial for certain data transformations or calculations.

functions.name: arraySome
functions.summary: The `arraySome` function iterates over an array and applies a given predicate function to each element, returning `true` if any element satisfies the predicate condition, and `false` otherwise. It is useful for quickly checking if at least one element in the array meets a specific criterion without relying on shorthand iteratee syntax.

functions.name: asciiToArray
functions.summary: The `asciiToArray` function takes an ASCII string as input and converts it into an array of individual characters. This can be useful for manipulating or processing each character separately in tasks such as text analysis or transformation.

functions.name: asciiWords
functions.summary: The `asciiWords` function takes an ASCII string as input and returns an array of its words by using a regular expression to match word patterns. This function is useful for text processing tasks where extracting individual words from a string is needed, such as for analysis or manipulation of textual data.

functions.name: baseFindKey
functions.summary: The `baseFindKey` function iterates over a given collection (array or object) using a specified iteration function (`eachFunc`) and applies a predicate function to each element; it returns the key of the first element that satisfies the predicate. This function is useful for finding the key of an element that meets certain criteria without relying on shorthand notations, serving as a foundational utility for methods like `_.findKey` and `_.findLastKey`.

functions.name: baseFindIndex
functions.summary: The `baseFindIndex` function searches through an array to find the index of the first element that satisfies a given predicate function, starting from a specified index and optionally searching from the end of the array. This utility is useful for efficiently locating elements based on custom conditions without the overhead of additional features like shorthand iteratee support.

functions.name: baseIndexOf
functions.summary: The `baseIndexOf` function searches for a specified value within an array starting from a given index and returns the index of the first occurrence of that value, or `-1` if the value is not found. It handles special cases for `NaN` values and is typically used as a foundational method for more complex indexing operations in libraries like Lodash.

functions.name: baseIndexOfWith
functions.summary: The `baseIndexOfWith` function searches for a specified value in an array starting from a given index, using a custom comparator function to determine equality. This allows for more flexible comparisons beyond strict equality, making it useful for scenarios where values may need to be compared based on specific criteria or properties.

functions.name: baseIsNaN
functions.summary: The `baseIsNaN` function checks if a given value is `NaN` (Not-a-Number) by leveraging the fact that `NaN` is the only value in JavaScript that is not equal to itself. This function is useful for accurately identifying `NaN` values without considering other number types, making it a foundational utility for more complex validation scenarios.

functions.name: baseMean
functions.summary: The `baseMean` function calculates the mean (average) of the values in a given array, applying a specified iteratee function to each element before summing them. It is a foundational implementation used in lodash's `_.mean` and `_.meanBy` methods, providing a way to compute averages while allowing for custom transformations of the array elements.

functions.name: baseProperty
functions.summary: The `baseProperty` function takes a string `key` as an argument and returns a new function that retrieves the value of the specified property from a given object. This utility is useful for creating accessor functions that can be used in contexts like sorting or mapping, where you need to extract property values from objects without directly referencing them each time.

functions.name: basePropertyOf
functions.summary: The `basePropertyOf` function takes an object as an argument and returns a new function that retrieves the value associated with a given key from that object. This is useful for creating accessor functions that can safely handle cases where the object may be null or undefined, preventing runtime errors when attempting to access properties.

functions.name: baseReduce
functions.signature: function baseReduce(collection, iteratee, accumulator, initAccum, eachFunc)
functions.summary: The `baseReduce` function iterates over a given collection, applying an `iteratee` function to accumulate a result based on the values in the collection. It allows for an optional initial accumulator value and is primarily used as a foundational implementation for the `_.reduce` and `_.reduceRight` methods in JavaScript, providing a way to transform collections into a single output value.

functions.name: baseSortBy
functions.summary: The `baseSortBy` function sorts an array based on a provided comparison function and then replaces each element in the sorted array with its corresponding `value` property. This function is useful for sorting complex objects by specific criteria while simplifying the output to just the desired values.

functions.name: baseSum
functions.summary: The `baseSum` function calculates the sum of values in an array after applying a specified transformation function (iteratee) to each element. It is useful for scenarios where you need to aggregate values based on a custom logic defined by the iteratee, while gracefully handling undefined results.

functions.name: baseTimes
functions.summary: The `baseTimes` function takes a number `n` and a function `iteratee`, invoking the `iteratee` function `n` times with the current index as an argument, and returns an array containing the results of these invocations. This function is useful for generating arrays based on a specified number of iterations, allowing for dynamic creation of data structures or values based on the index.

functions.name: baseToPairs
functions.summary: The `baseToPairs` function takes an object and an array of property names, returning an array of key-value pairs where each pair consists of a property name and its corresponding value from the object. This function is useful for transforming an object's specified properties into a more manageable format for further processing or analysis.

functions.name: baseTrim
functions.summary: The `baseTrim` function removes leading and trailing whitespace from a given string, returning the trimmed result. It is a private implementation, likely used internally to ensure consistent string formatting in applications where whitespace handling is important.

functions.name: baseUnary
functions.summary: The `baseUnary` function takes a single argument function `func` and returns a new function that accepts only one argument, effectively capping the number of arguments to one. This is useful for creating functions that conform to a unary function signature, ensuring that they only process a single input value.

functions.name: baseValues
functions.summary: The `baseValues` function takes an object and an array of property names, returning an array of the corresponding values from the object for those properties. This utility is useful for extracting specific values from an object based on a predefined list of keys.

functions.name: cacheHas
functions.summary: The `cacheHas` function checks if a specified `key` exists in a given `cache` object, returning `true` if the entry is present and `false` otherwise. This function is useful for efficiently determining the existence of cached data before attempting to retrieve or manipulate it.

functions.name: charsStartIndex
functions.summary: The `charsStartIndex` function determines the index of the first character in the `strSymbols` array that is not present in the `chrSymbols` array. This is useful for trimming operations, as it helps identify where the meaningful content of a string begins by skipping over specified leading characters.

functions.name: charsEndIndex
functions.summary: The `charsEndIndex` function determines the index of the last character in an array of string symbols (`strSymbols`) that is not present in a specified array of character symbols (`chrSymbols`). It is primarily used by the `_.trim` and `_.trimEnd` functions to identify where to stop trimming characters from the end of a string.

functions.name: countHolders
functions.summary: The `countHolders` function counts and returns the number of times a specified `placeholder` appears in a given `array`. This function is useful for determining the frequency of a specific value within an array, which can be helpful in data analysis or validation scenarios.

functions.name: escapeStringChar
functions.summary: The `escapeStringChar` function takes a character as input and returns its escaped version by prefixing it with a backslash, utilizing a predefined mapping of characters in `stringEscapes`. This function is typically used in template compilation to ensure that special characters are properly escaped for inclusion in string literals, preventing syntax errors or unintended behavior.

functions.name: getValue
functions.summary: The `getValue` function retrieves the value associated with a specified `key` from a given `object`, returning `undefined` if the `object` is `null` or `undefined`. This utility is useful for safely accessing properties without throwing errors when the object is not defined.

functions.name: hasUnicode
functions.summary: The `hasUnicode` function checks if a given string contains any Unicode symbols by testing it against a predefined regular expression. This function is useful for applications that need to identify or handle strings with special characters beyond the basic ASCII set.

functions.name: hasUnicodeWord
functions.summary: The `hasUnicodeWord` function checks if a given string contains any words made up of Unicode symbols, returning `true` if such a word is found and `false` otherwise. This function is useful for validating text input that may include diverse character sets beyond standard ASCII, ensuring proper handling of internationalization or special symbols.

functions.name: iteratorToArray
functions.summary: The `iteratorToArray` function converts an iterator into an array by repeatedly calling the iterator's `next` method and collecting its values until it reaches the end. This is useful for transforming iterable data structures into a more manageable array format for easier manipulation and access.

functions.name: mapToArray
functions.summary: The `mapToArray` function converts a Map object into an array of its key-value pairs, where each pair is represented as a two-element array. This is useful for scenarios where you need to manipulate or iterate over the entries of a Map in a format that is compatible with array methods.

functions.name: overArg
functions.summary: The `overArg` function creates a new unary function that applies a specified transformation to its argument before passing it to the original function. This is useful for modifying input data on-the-fly, allowing for cleaner and more modular code when dealing with functions that require specific argument formats.

functions.name: replaceHolders
functions.summary: The `replaceHolders` function replaces all instances of a specified `placeholder` in the given `array` with an internal constant `PLACEHOLDER`, while also collecting and returning the indexes of the replaced elements. This can be useful for tracking the positions of placeholders in an array for further processing or manipulation.

functions.name: setToArray
functions.summary: The `setToArray` function converts a Set object into an array containing its values, allowing for easier manipulation and access to the Set's elements in array form. This is useful when you need to perform array-specific operations on the values stored in a Set.

functions.name: setToPairs
functions.summary: The `setToPairs` function converts a Set object into an array of value-value pairs, where each pair consists of the same value from the set. This can be useful for scenarios where a consistent structure of pairs is needed for further processing or manipulation of the set's values.

functions.name: strictIndexOf
functions.summary: The `strictIndexOf` function searches for the first occurrence of a specified value in an array, starting from a given index, using strict equality (`===`) for comparison. It returns the index of the matched value or `-1` if the value is not found, making it useful for precise value searches in arrays where type and value must match exactly.

functions.name: strictLastIndexOf
functions.summary: The `strictLastIndexOf` function searches for the last occurrence of a specified value in an array, starting from a given index, and uses strict equality (`===`) for comparisons. It is useful for scenarios where precise value matching is required, such as distinguishing between different types or instances.

functions.name: stringSize
functions.summary: The `stringSize` function calculates and returns the number of symbols in a given string, distinguishing between Unicode and ASCII characters to ensure accurate counting. This is useful for applications that need to handle text with varying character encodings, such as user input validation or text processing.

functions.name: stringToArray
functions.summary: The `stringToArray` function converts a given string into an array, handling both Unicode and ASCII characters appropriately by delegating to specific conversion functions based on the string's encoding. This is useful for processing strings in a way that accommodates different character sets, ensuring compatibility and proper handling of diverse text inputs.

functions.name: trimmedEndIndex
functions.summary: The `trimmedEndIndex` function calculates and returns the index of the last non-whitespace character in a given string. This is useful for trimming operations, as it helps identify where to stop when removing trailing whitespace from the string.

functions.name: unicodeSize
functions.summary: The `unicodeSize` function calculates the number of Unicode characters in a given string by using a regular expression to match each character and incrementing a counter for each match. This is useful for accurately determining the length of strings that may contain multi-byte Unicode characters, ensuring proper handling of text in applications that require precise character counts.

functions.name: unicodeToArray
functions.summary: The `unicodeToArray` function converts a Unicode string into an array of its individual Unicode code points by using a regular expression (`reUnicode`) to match the characters. This is useful for processing or manipulating Unicode characters in a more granular way, such as when handling text that includes emojis or characters from various languages.

functions.name: unicodeWords
functions.summary: The `unicodeWords` function takes a Unicode string as input and returns an array of its words by matching them against a predefined regular expression (`reUnicodeWord`). This function is useful for extracting words from strings that may contain a variety of Unicode characters, ensuring accurate word separation in diverse languages and scripts.

functions.name: lodash
functions.docstring:
Creates a `lodash` object which wraps `value` to enable implicit method
chain sequences. Methods that operate on and return arrays, collections,
and functions can be chained together. Methods that retrieve a single value
or may return a primitive value will automatically end the chain sequence
and return the unwrapped value. Otherwise, the value must be unwrapped
with `_#value`.
Explicit chain sequences, which must be unwrapped with `_#value`, may be
enabled using `_.chain`.
The execution of chained methods is lazy, that is, it's deferred until
`_#value` is implicitly or explicitly called.
Lazy evaluation allows several methods to support shortcut fusion.
Shortcut fusion is an optimization to merge iteratee calls; this avoids
the creation of intermediate arrays and can greatly reduce the number of
iteratee executions. Sections of a chain sequence qualify for shortcut
fusion if the section is applied to an array and iteratees accept only
one argument. The heuristic for whether a section qualifies for shortcut
fusion is subject to change.
Chaining is supported in custom builds as long as the `_#value` method is
directly or indirectly included in the build.
In addition to lodash methods, wrappers have `Array` and `String` methods.
The wrapper `Array` methods are:
`concat`, `join`, `pop`, `push`, `shift`, `sort`, `splice`, and `unshift`
The wrapper `String` methods are:
`replace` and `split`
The wrapper methods that support shortcut fusion are:
`at`, `compact`, `drop`, `dropRight`, `dropWhile`, `filter`, `find`,
`findLast`, `head`, `initial`, `last`, `map`, `reject`, `reverse`, `slice`,
`tail`, `take`, `takeRight`, `takeRightWhile`, `takeWhile`, and `toArray`
The chainable wrapper methods are:
`after`, `ary`, `assign`, `assignIn`, `assignInWith`, `assignWith`, `at`,
`before`, `bind`, `bindAll`, `bindKey`, `castArray`, `chain`, `chunk`,

@name _
@constructor
@category Seq
@param {*} value The value to wrap in a `lodash` instance.
@returns {Object} Returns the new `lodash` wrapper instance.
@example
function square(n) {
  return n * n;
}
var wrapped = _([1, 2, 3]);
// Returns an unwrapped value.
wrapped.reduce(_.add);
// => 6
// Returns a wrapped value.
var squares = wrapped.map(square);
_.isArray(squares);
// => false
_.isArray(squares.value());
// => true
functions.summary: The `lodash` function creates a `LodashWrapper` object that wraps a given value, enabling method chaining for operations on arrays, collections, and functions. This allows users to perform multiple operations in a concise and readable manner, enhancing code efficiency and clarity.

functions.name: object
functions.code: function object() {}
functions.summary: The `object` function is an empty JavaScript function that does not perform any actions or return any values. It may be used as a placeholder or for defining a function that can be expanded later, or it could serve as a constructor for creating objects if modified.

functions.name: baseLodash
functions.docstring:
The function whose prototype chain sequence wrappers inherit from.
@private
functions.summary: The `baseLodash` function is an empty constructor that serves as a foundational prototype for sequence wrappers in the Lodash library. It is designed to provide a base for creating objects that inherit from it, facilitating the implementation of various utility functions without performing any operations itself.

functions.name: LodashWrapper
functions.summary: The `LodashWrapper` function is a constructor for creating wrapper objects in the Lodash library, which encapsulate a value and allow for method chaining. It initializes properties to manage the wrapped value, track actions, and control chaining behavior, enabling users to perform a sequence of operations on the wrapped data in a fluent style.

functions.name: LazyWrapper
functions.summary: The `LazyWrapper` function creates an object that wraps a given value to facilitate lazy evaluation, allowing for deferred computation of operations on that value. This is useful for optimizing performance by postponing execution until the result is actually needed, thereby potentially reducing unnecessary calculations.

functions.name: lazyClone
functions.summary: The `lazyClone` function creates a duplicate of a `LazyWrapper` object, preserving its internal state and properties such as actions, direction, filters, iteratees, take count, and views. This is useful for maintaining the original object's configuration while allowing for independent modifications or operations on the cloned instance.

functions.name: lazyReverse
functions.summary: The `lazyReverse` function reverses the direction of lazy iteration in a `LazyWrapper` object, allowing for efficient traversal of data in the opposite order. It is useful for scenarios where the order of processing needs to be changed without creating a new data set, thereby maintaining performance in data manipulation.

functions.name: lazyValue
functions.summary: The `lazyValue` function extracts and processes the unwrapped value from a lazy wrapper, applying specified iteratees to filter or map the elements based on defined conditions. It is used to efficiently handle operations on large datasets by delaying execution until necessary, optimizing performance in scenarios where only a subset of data is needed.

functions.name: Hash
functions.summary: The `Hash` function creates a hash object that stores key-value pairs, initializing it with optional entries provided as an array. This is useful for efficiently caching and retrieving data based on unique keys.

functions.name: hashClear
functions.summary: The `hashClear` function resets a hash object by removing all key-value entries, effectively initializing it to an empty state. This is useful for freeing up memory or preparing the hash for reuse without creating a new instance.

functions.name: hashDelete
functions.summary: The `hashDelete` function removes a specified key and its associated value from a hash object, returning `true` if the deletion was successful and `false` otherwise. This function is useful for managing dynamic data structures where entries may need to be removed as part of data manipulation or cleanup processes.

functions.name: hashGet
functions.summary: The `hashGet` function retrieves the value associated with a specified `key` from a hash-like data structure, returning `undefined` if the key does not exist or if its value is marked as `HASH_UNDEFINED`. This function is useful for accessing stored values efficiently in a hash table implementation.

functions.name: hashHas
functions.summary: The `hashHas` function checks whether a hash value associated with a given `key` exists in the object's internal data structure. It returns `true` if the entry is present and `false` otherwise, making it useful for verifying the existence of specific entries in a hash map.

functions.name: hashSet
functions.summary: The `hashSet` function sets a specified `key` in a hash table to a given `value`, updating the size of the hash table accordingly. It is used to store key-value pairs in a data structure, allowing for efficient retrieval and management of data.

functions.name: ListCache
functions.summary: The `ListCache` function creates a cache object that stores key-value pairs provided in the `entries` array. It initializes the cache by clearing any existing entries and populating it with the specified key-value pairs, making it useful for efficiently managing and retrieving data in a structured format.

functions.name: listCacheClear
functions.summary: The `listCacheClear` function clears all key-value entries from a list cache by resetting its internal data structure to an empty array and setting its size to zero. This function is typically used to efficiently remove all cached entries, allowing for fresh data storage in scenarios where the cache needs to be reset.

functions.name: listCacheDelete
functions.summary: The `listCacheDelete` function removes a specified key and its associated value from a list cache, returning `true` if the entry was successfully deleted and `false` if the key was not found. This function is useful for managing cached data by allowing users to efficiently remove entries when they are no longer needed.

functions.name: listCacheGet
functions.summary: The `listCacheGet` function retrieves the value associated with a specified `key` from a list cache, returning `undefined` if the key does not exist. This function is useful for efficiently accessing cached data in scenarios where quick lookups are necessary.

functions.name: listCacheHas
functions.summary: The `listCacheHas` function checks if a specific entry identified by `key` exists in a list cache. It returns `true` if the entry is found, allowing users to verify the presence of cached data efficiently.

functions.name: listCacheSet
functions.summary: The `listCacheSet` function sets a specified `key` to a given `value` in a list cache, either adding a new entry or updating an existing one. This function is useful for efficiently managing key-value pairs in a cache-like structure, allowing for quick retrieval and modification of stored data.

functions.name: MapCache
functions.summary: The `MapCache` function creates a cache object for storing key-value pairs, initializing it with optional entries provided as an array. This allows for efficient retrieval and management of data, making it useful for scenarios where quick access to stored values is needed.

functions.name: mapCacheClear
functions.summary: The `mapCacheClear` function clears all key-value entries from a map by resetting its size to zero and reinitializing its internal data structure. This is useful for efficiently managing memory and ensuring that the map is empty before reuse.

functions.name: mapCacheDelete
functions.summary: The `mapCacheDelete` function removes a specified key and its associated value from a map, updating the map's size accordingly. It returns `true` if the entry was successfully deleted, or `false` if the key was not found, making it useful for managing dynamic data stored in a map structure.

functions.name: mapCacheGet
functions.summary: The `mapCacheGet` function retrieves the value associated with a specified `key` from a map data structure. It is used to access stored values efficiently, typically within a caching mechanism to improve performance by avoiding redundant computations.

functions.name: mapCacheHas
functions.summary: The `mapCacheHas` function checks whether a specific key exists in a map data structure associated with the current instance of `MapCache`. It returns `true` if the key is found, allowing users to verify the presence of an entry before performing further operations.

functions.name: mapCacheSet
functions.summary: The `mapCacheSet` function sets a specified `key` to a given `value` in a map cache, updating the cache's size if the key is new. This function is useful for managing key-value pairs in a cache structure, ensuring efficient storage and retrieval of data.

functions.name: SetCache
functions.summary: The `SetCache` function creates an array cache object that stores unique values using a `MapCache` for efficient retrieval. It is designed to optimize performance by preventing duplicate entries when initializing the cache with a provided array of values.

functions.name: cloneDataView
functions.summary: The `cloneDataView` function creates a clone of a given `dataView`, optionally performing a deep clone of its underlying `ArrayBuffer`. This is useful for creating independent copies of data views in scenarios where modifications to one view should not affect the other.

functions.name: cloneRegExp
functions.summary: The `cloneRegExp` function creates a duplicate of a given regular expression object, preserving its source, flags, and last index. This is useful for scenarios where you need to maintain the original regex's state while allowing modifications or reusability without affecting the original instance.

functions.name: cloneSymbol
functions.summary: The `cloneSymbol` function creates a clone of a given symbol object by invoking its internal `valueOf` method, returning a new symbol if available; otherwise, it returns an empty object. This function is useful for scenarios where a distinct copy of a symbol is needed without altering the original symbol's state or properties.

functions.name: cloneTypedArray
functions.summary: The `cloneTypedArray` function creates a clone of a given typed array, optionally performing a deep clone of its underlying buffer if specified. This is useful for creating independent copies of typed arrays, ensuring that modifications to the clone do not affect the original array.

functions.name: compareAscending
functions.summary: The `compareAscending` function compares two values to determine their sort order in ascending order, returning -1 if the first value is less than the second, 1 if it is greater, and 0 if they are considered equal. This function is useful for sorting algorithms that require a custom comparison logic, particularly when dealing with various data types, including undefined, null, and symbols.

functions.name: compareMultiple
functions.summary: The `compareMultiple` function compares multiple properties of two objects for sorting purposes, allowing for both ascending and descending order based on the specified `orders` array. It is primarily used to facilitate stable sorting in the `_.orderBy` function, ensuring consistent results across different JavaScript engines.

functions.name: composeArgs
functions.summary: The `composeArgs` function creates a new array that combines partially applied arguments, placeholders, and provided arguments into a single array, effectively allowing for the construction of a complete set of arguments for a function call. This is useful in functional programming contexts, particularly for currying and partial application, where you want to pre-fill some arguments while leaving others to be supplied later.

functions.name: composeArgsRight
functions.summary: The `composeArgsRight` function combines a given array of arguments (`args`) with additional arguments (`partials`) to be appended at the end, while also handling placeholders (`holders`) that indicate where to insert elements from `args`. This is particularly useful for creating partially applied functions in a right-to-left manner, allowing for more flexible function composition in JavaScript.

functions.name: copyArray
functions.summary: The `copyArray` function copies the elements from a source array to a target array, initializing the target array if it is not provided. This function is useful for duplicating array contents without modifying the original array, ensuring that the target array contains the same values as the source.

functions.name: copyObject
functions.summary: The `copyObject` function copies specified properties from a `source` object to a target `object`, allowing for an optional `customizer` function to modify the values during the copy process. This function is useful for selectively transferring properties while providing flexibility in how those properties are assigned, making it ideal for scenarios where object merging or transformation is needed.

functions.name: copySymbols
functions.summary: The `copySymbols` function copies the own symbol properties from a specified `source` object to a target `object`, returning the updated target object. This is useful for ensuring that symbol properties, which are often used for unique object keys, are transferred between objects while maintaining encapsulation and avoiding property name collisions.

functions.name: copySymbolsIn
functions.summary: The `copySymbolsIn` function copies both the own and inherited symbol properties from a specified `source` object to a target `object`, returning the updated target object. This is useful for ensuring that all symbol properties, which are not included in regular property enumerations, are transferred, preserving the complete set of unique properties in scenarios where symbol properties are significant.

functions.name: createAggregator
functions.summary: The `createAggregator` function generates a custom aggregation function that groups elements of a collection based on a specified setter function, with an optional initializer for the accumulator object. This is useful for creating tailored aggregation behaviors similar to `_.groupBy` in lodash, allowing developers to efficiently organize data based on specific criteria.

functions.name: createAssigner
functions.summary: The `createAssigner` function generates a new function that assigns properties from source objects to a target object using a specified assignment strategy defined by the `assigner` function. This utility is useful for creating customized object merging behaviors, such as deep merging or conditional property assignment, while also allowing for optional customizers and guards.

functions.name: createBaseEach
functions.summary: The `createBaseEach` function generates a custom iterator function that applies a specified iteration function (`eachFunc`) to elements of a collection, allowing for optional right-to-left traversal. This is useful for creating flexible iteration methods that can handle different types of collections while providing control over the iteration direction.

functions.name: createBaseFor
functions.summary: The `createBaseFor` function generates a base iteration function that can be used with methods like `_.forIn` and `_.forOwn` to iterate over the properties of an object. It allows for optional iteration direction (from right to left) and applies a provided callback function (`iteratee`) to each property, stopping if the callback returns `false`.

functions.name: createBind
functions.summary: The `createBind` function creates a new function that wraps the provided `func`, allowing it to be invoked with a specific `this` context defined by `thisArg` if the binding flag is set. This is useful for ensuring that the function retains the desired context when called, particularly in scenarios where the context may change, such as in event handlers or callbacks.

functions.name: createCaseFirst
functions.summary: The `createCaseFirst` function generates a new function that modifies the first character of a given string using a specified string case method (like converting to lowercase or uppercase). This is useful for creating consistent string formatting in applications where the first character's case needs to be adjusted while preserving the rest of the string.

functions.name: createCompounder
functions.summary: The `createCompounder` function generates a new function that transforms a given string into a compound word format (like camelCase) by applying a specified callback to each word in the string. This is useful for creating custom string formatting functions that combine words in various ways, leveraging the provided callback for the desired transformation.

functions.name: createCtor
functions.summary: The `createCtor` function generates a new constructor function that allows instances of the provided constructor (`Ctor`) to be created regardless of how the function is invoked—whether with the `new` keyword or using `call` or `apply`. This is useful for ensuring consistent behavior when creating instances, particularly in scenarios where the invocation context may vary.

functions.name: createCurry
functions.summary: The `createCurry` function wraps a given function to enable currying, allowing it to be called with fewer arguments than required, and returns a new function that can be invoked with partial arguments until all required arguments are provided. This is useful for creating more flexible and reusable functions by breaking down the argument requirements into smaller, manageable pieces.

functions.name: createFind
functions.summary: The `createFind` function generates a new function that locates the index of an element in a collection based on a specified predicate, allowing for both standard and last-find operations. This is useful for efficiently searching through arrays or objects to retrieve specific values based on custom criteria.

functions.name: createFlow
functions.summary: The `createFlow` function generates a new function that composes multiple functions together, allowing them to be executed in a specified order (either left-to-right or right-to-left) based on the `fromRight` parameter. This is useful for creating a sequence of operations that can be applied to a value, facilitating functional programming patterns and code reusability.

functions.name: createHybrid
functions.signature: function createHybrid(func, bitmask, thisArg, partials, holders, partialsRight, holdersRight, argPos, ary, arity)
functions.summary: The `createHybrid` function creates a versatile wrapper around a given function (`func`), allowing for optional features such as `this` binding, partial application of arguments, currying, and argument flipping based on specified bitmask flags. This enables developers to create highly customizable function behaviors, facilitating more flexible and reusable code in JavaScript applications.

functions.name: createInverter
functions.summary: The `createInverter` function generates a new function that inverts an object's properties based on a specified iteratee and a setter function for the accumulator values. This is useful for transforming data structures by reversing key-value pairs according to custom logic defined by the provided functions.

functions.name: createMathOperation
functions.summary: The `createMathOperation` function generates a new function that applies a specified mathematical operation (provided as the `operator` argument) to two input values, while also handling cases where either value may be `undefined` by returning a `defaultValue` if both are `undefined`. This utility is useful for creating flexible mathematical operations that can accommodate missing inputs gracefully.

functions.name: createOver
functions.summary: The `createOver` function generates a new function that applies a specified `arrayFunc` to a list of iteratee functions, allowing for the simultaneous invocation of multiple functions with the same arguments. This is useful for scenarios where you want to execute several operations in parallel, such as combining results from different computations.

functions.name: createPadding
functions.summary: The `createPadding` function generates a padding string of a specified length using a given character string, truncating the character string if necessary. It is useful for formatting strings to ensure they have a consistent length, often for display purposes in user interfaces or text outputs.

functions.name: createPartial
functions.summary: The `createPartial` function creates a new function that invokes a specified function (`func`) with a specific `this` context (`thisArg`) and a set of predefined arguments (`partials`) added to the front of any arguments passed to the new function. This allows for easier function customization and reuse by pre-filling certain parameters while maintaining the ability to pass additional arguments at invocation.

functions.name: createRange
functions.summary: The `createRange` function generates a new range function that can create arrays of numbers within a specified range, optionally iterating from right to left. This is useful for generating sequences of numbers with customizable start, end, and step values, allowing for flexible iteration in various programming scenarios.

functions.name: createRelationalOperation
functions.summary: The `createRelationalOperation` function takes a relational operator function as an argument and returns a new function that applies this operator to two values, converting them to numbers if they are not both strings. This is useful for creating consistent relational comparisons that handle both string and numeric inputs seamlessly.

functions.name: createRecurry
functions.signature: function createRecurry(func, bitmask, wrapFunc, placeholder, thisArg, partials, holders, argPos, ary, arity)
functions.summary: The `createRecurry` function generates a new function that allows for continued currying of the provided `func`, enabling partial application of arguments either from the left or right based on the specified bitmask flags. This is useful for creating more flexible and reusable function wrappers that can adapt to different argument configurations while maintaining the original function's behavior.

functions.name: createRound
functions.summary: The `createRound` function generates a custom rounding function based on a specified `Math` method (like `Math.round`, `Math.floor`, or `Math.ceil`), allowing for precise rounding of numbers to a specified number of decimal places while mitigating floating-point inaccuracies. This is useful for applications that require consistent and accurate numerical rounding behavior.

functions.name: createToPairs
functions.summary: The `createToPairs` function generates a new function that converts an object into an array of key-value pairs based on a provided `keysFunc` for retrieving the object's keys. This is useful for transforming different types of objects, such as maps and sets, into a consistent format for easier manipulation or iteration.

functions.name: createWrap
functions.signature: function createWrap(func, bitmask, thisArg, partials, holders, argPos, ary, arity)
functions.summary: The `createWrap` function constructs a new function that can either invoke or curry the provided `func`, with options for binding its context (`this`), applying partial arguments, and controlling the number of arguments expected. This utility is useful for creating flexible function wrappers that can adapt to various calling conventions and argument configurations, enhancing code reusability and modularity.

functions.name: customDefaultsAssignIn
functions.summary: The `customDefaultsAssignIn` function assigns the source value (`srcValue`) to a destination object property (`objValue`) only if the destination property's value is `undefined` or if it matches the default prototype value and the property does not exist on the object. This function is used to customize the behavior of `_.defaults` in lodash, ensuring that default values are assigned only when necessary.

functions.name: customDefaultsMerge
functions.signature: function customDefaultsMerge(objValue, srcValue, key, object, source, stack)
functions.summary: The `customDefaultsMerge` function is designed to recursively merge properties from a source object into a destination object, specifically when both values are objects. It is used internally by `_.defaultsDeep` to ensure that nested objects and arrays are merged correctly, allowing for a deep merging of default values into a target object while avoiding circular references.

functions.name: customOmitClone
functions.summary: The `customOmitClone` function checks if the provided `value` is a plain object; if it is, the function returns `undefined` to indicate that cloning should be deferred to `_.cloneDeep`, otherwise, it returns the original value. This customization is useful for optimizing cloning behavior in the `_.omit` function by only cloning plain objects, thereby improving performance and avoiding unnecessary cloning of non-plain objects.

functions.name: equalArrays
functions.signature: function equalArrays(array, other, bitmask, customizer, equalFunc, stack)
functions.summary: The `equalArrays` function compares two arrays for equality, supporting partial deep comparisons and handling cyclic references through a stack mechanism. It is useful for determining if two arrays are equivalent in content and structure, particularly in scenarios where custom comparison logic is needed or when dealing with unordered elements.

functions.name: equalByTag
functions.signature: function equalByTag(object, other, tag, bitmask, customizer, equalFunc, stack)
functions.summary: The `equalByTag` function compares two objects of the same `toStringTag` (such as Boolean, Date, Error, Number, RegExp, or String) for equality, handling specific data types and their unique properties. It is used to ensure accurate deep equality checks by considering the nuances of different object types, making it useful in scenarios where precise comparisons are necessary, such as in libraries for data manipulation or validation.

functions.name: equalObjects
functions.signature: function equalObjects(object, other, bitmask, customizer, equalFunc, stack)
functions.summary: The `equalObjects` function performs a deep comparison between two objects, allowing for partial matches based on specified bitmask flags and a custom comparison function. It is useful for determining object equality in scenarios where objects may not be fully identical but share certain properties, such as in libraries for data validation or state management.

functions.name: flatRest
functions.summary: The `flatRest` function creates a new function that applies a rest parameter to the provided `func`, flattening any nested arrays in the arguments. This is useful for simplifying the handling of variable-length arguments, especially when dealing with arrays that may contain additional nested arrays.

functions.name: getAllKeys
functions.summary: The `getAllKeys` function retrieves an array of all own enumerable property names and symbols from a given object. This is useful for developers who need to inspect or manipulate the properties of an object, including both standard keys and symbol keys, in a comprehensive manner.

functions.name: getAllKeysIn
functions.summary: The `getAllKeysIn` function retrieves an array of all enumerable property names and symbols, both own and inherited, from a given object. This is useful for developers who need to inspect or manipulate all properties of an object, including those inherited from its prototype chain.

functions.name: getFuncName
functions.summary: The `getFuncName` function retrieves the name of a given function, checking against a predefined mapping of function names to ensure accuracy. It is useful for debugging or logging purposes, where knowing the exact name of a function is important for clarity and traceability.

functions.name: getHolder
functions.summary: The `getHolder` function retrieves the placeholder value associated with a given function, typically used in the context of libraries like Lodash that support placeholder functionality for partial application. This is useful for developers who want to utilize placeholders in their function compositions or currying to enhance code readability and flexibility.

functions.name: getIteratee
functions.summary: The `getIteratee` function retrieves the appropriate iteratee function, either a custom one defined in `lodash.iteratee` or a default `baseIteratee`, and invokes it with provided arguments if any are given. This allows for flexible handling of data transformations or iterations in a consistent manner, accommodating user-defined behavior when necessary.

functions.name: getMapData
functions.summary: The `getMapData` function retrieves the data associated with a specified key from a given map object, differentiating between string and non-string keys to access the appropriate data structure. This function is useful for efficiently accessing stored values in a map-like structure, particularly in scenarios where the map's internal data organization varies based on the key type.

functions.name: getMatchData
functions.summary: The `getMatchData` function retrieves the property names and values of a given object, along with a flag indicating whether each value is strictly comparable. This is useful for comparing objects in a way that respects their properties and types, facilitating tasks such as deep equality checks or filtering.

functions.name: getNative
functions.summary: The `getNative` function retrieves a method from a specified object by its key and checks if that method is a native function. It returns the method if it is native; otherwise, it returns `undefined`, which is useful for ensuring that only built-in functions are accessed, potentially for safety or compatibility reasons.

functions.name: getRawTag
functions.summary: The `getRawTag` function retrieves the raw `toStringTag` of a given value while ignoring any custom `Symbol.toStringTag` properties. It is useful for accurately identifying the type of an object without interference from user-defined tags, ensuring consistent type checking in JavaScript.

functions.name: getView
functions.summary: The `getView` function adjusts the `start` and `end` positions based on a series of transformations specified in the `transforms` array, which can include operations like dropping or taking elements from either end of the view. This function is useful for dynamically modifying a range of data based on specific criteria or requirements.

functions.name: getWrapDetails
functions.summary: The `getWrapDetails` function extracts wrapper details from a given source string by matching it against a regular expression and splitting the captured details into an array. This function is useful for parsing and retrieving structured information from comments in code, particularly in scenarios where wrappers or decorators are documented in a specific format.

functions.name: hasPath
functions.summary: The `hasPath` function checks if a specified path exists within a given object, using a provided function to verify the presence of each key along the path. This is useful for safely accessing deeply nested properties in an object without encountering errors if any part of the path is undefined or does not exist.

functions.name: initCloneArray
functions.summary: The `initCloneArray` function creates a new array instance that is a clone of the provided array, preserving its length and specific properties if the first element is a string and the array has an `index` property (typically found in regex match results). This function is useful for initializing a new array that maintains certain characteristics of the original, particularly in scenarios involving regular expression operations.

functions.name: initCloneObject
functions.summary: The `initCloneObject` function creates a clone of a given object by checking if the object's constructor is a function and if it is not a prototype; if both conditions are met, it uses `baseCreate` to create a new object with the same prototype as the original, otherwise, it returns an empty object. This function is useful for ensuring that cloned objects maintain their prototype chain when duplicating complex objects.

functions.name: initCloneByTag
functions.summary: The `initCloneByTag` function creates a clone of a given object based on its `toStringTag`, supporting specific types like `Boolean`, `Date`, `Map`, `Number`, `RegExp`, `Set`, and `String`. This function is useful for ensuring accurate cloning of complex objects while preserving their type-specific behaviors and properties.

functions.name: insertWrapDetails
functions.summary: The `insertWrapDetails` function modifies a given source string by inserting a comment at the top of its body, indicating the details of the wrapper used. This is useful for documentation purposes, allowing developers to easily identify how the source has been wrapped or modified.

functions.name: isFlattenable
functions.summary: The `isFlattenable` function checks if a given value is either an array, an `arguments` object, or an object that has a specific `spreadableSymbol` property, indicating it can be flattened. This function is useful for determining whether a value can be safely flattened into a single array, which is often needed in operations that involve merging or combining data structures.

functions.name: isIndex
functions.summary: The `isIndex` function checks if a given value is a valid array-like index, ensuring it is a non-negative integer that falls within the specified bounds (defaulting to `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`). This function is useful for validating indices before accessing elements in an array or array-like structure, preventing potential errors from invalid index usage.

functions.name: isIterateeCall
functions.summary: The `isIterateeCall` function checks if the provided arguments correspond to a valid iteratee call, verifying that the `object` is indeed an object and that the `index` is either a valid numeric index or a string key present in the `object`. This function is useful for ensuring that a value is being accessed correctly within the context of a collection iteration, helping to prevent errors in functional programming scenarios.

functions.name: isKey
functions.summary: The `isKey` function checks if a given `value` is a valid property name (not a property path) for an object, returning `true` if it is. This is useful for ensuring that a value can be safely used as a key when accessing properties on an object, avoiding potential errors with nested property paths.

functions.name: isKeyable
functions.summary: The `isKeyable` function determines if a given value can be used as a unique key for an object, returning `true` for strings, numbers, symbols, and booleans (excluding the special case of `'__proto__'`), as well as for `null`. This is useful for ensuring that only valid keys are used when creating or manipulating objects in JavaScript.

functions.name: isLaziable
functions.summary: The `isLaziable` function checks if a given function (`func`) has a corresponding lazy version in the Lodash library by verifying its name and comparing it to the functions available in the `LazyWrapper` prototype. This is useful for determining if a function can be optimized for lazy evaluation, which can improve performance by deferring execution until necessary.

functions.name: isMasked
functions.summary: The `isMasked` function determines whether a given function `func` has its source code masked by checking for the presence of a specific key (`maskSrcKey`) in the function. This is useful for identifying functions that may have been altered or obscured, which can be important for debugging or ensuring code integrity.

functions.name: isPrototype
functions.summary: The `isPrototype` function checks if a given value is likely a prototype object by comparing it to the prototype of its constructor. It is useful for determining if an object serves as a prototype in JavaScript's prototypal inheritance system.

functions.name: isStrictComparable
functions.summary: The `isStrictComparable` function checks if a given value is suitable for strict equality comparisons (`===`) by verifying that the value is not an object and that it is equal to itself (which rules out `NaN`). This function is useful for determining if a value can be reliably compared without the complications that arise from objects or special cases like `NaN`.

functions.name: matchesStrictComparable
functions.summary: The `matchesStrictComparable` function creates a predicate function that checks if a given object has a specified property with a value that strictly equals a provided source value. This is useful for filtering or matching objects in collections based on exact property-value pairs, ensuring that comparisons handle `undefined` values correctly.

functions.name: memoizeCapped
functions.summary: The `memoizeCapped` function creates a memoized version of a given function that caches its results for efficiency, but clears the cache when the number of stored results exceeds a predefined limit (`MAX_MEMOIZE_SIZE`). This is useful for optimizing performance in scenarios where a function is called frequently with the same arguments, while preventing excessive memory usage.

functions.name: mergeData
functions.summary: The `mergeData` function combines the metadata of a `source` function into a `data` function to optimize function invocation by reducing the number of wrappers applied. This is useful for enhancing performance and flexibility when working with function utilities like binding, currying, and partial application in JavaScript.

functions.name: nativeKeysIn
functions.summary: The `nativeKeysIn` function retrieves an array of all enumerable property names from a given object, including those inherited from its prototype chain. This is useful for scenarios where you need a comprehensive list of properties, not just those defined directly on the object itself.

functions.name: objectToString
functions.summary: The `objectToString` function converts any given value into a string representation by utilizing `Object.prototype.toString`. This is useful for accurately determining the type of the value, especially for distinguishing between different object types in JavaScript.

functions.name: overRest
functions.summary: The `overRest` function creates a new function that applies a specified transformation to the rest parameters of the original function, starting from a given index. This allows for customized handling of additional arguments when invoking the original function, making it useful for scenarios where you want to preprocess or modify the rest parameters before passing them along.

functions.name: parent
functions.summary: The `parent` function retrieves the parent value of a specified path within a given object. It is useful for navigating complex nested structures, allowing users to access the value that is one level up from the specified path.

functions.name: reorder
functions.summary: The `reorder` function rearranges the elements of a given array based on the specified indexes, effectively creating a new order where each element is placed according to its corresponding index from the `indexes` array. This function is useful for scenarios where you need to reorder data, such as sorting items based on a predefined sequence or mapping elements to a specific arrangement.

functions.name: safeGet
functions.summary: The `safeGet` function retrieves the value of a specified property from an object, while preventing access to potentially harmful properties like `__proto__` and `constructor`. This is useful for ensuring safe property access and avoiding unintended behavior or security issues in JavaScript applications.

functions.name: setWrapToString
functions.summary: The `setWrapToString` function modifies the `toString` method of a given `wrapper` function to reflect the source code of a `reference` function, while also including additional details about the wrapper in a comment. This is useful for maintaining clarity and transparency in debugging or when inspecting the wrapper function, as it helps convey its purpose and relationship to the original reference function.

functions.name: shortOut
functions.summary: The `shortOut` function creates a wrapper around a given function that limits its execution by invoking an `identity` function (returning the first argument) if the wrapped function is called `HOT_COUNT` or more times within a specified `HOT_SPAN` milliseconds. This is useful for optimizing performance by preventing excessive calls to a potentially expensive function during high-frequency events.

functions.name: shuffleSelf
functions.summary: The `shuffleSelf` function randomly shuffles the elements of a given array and truncates its length to a specified size, mutating the original array in the process. This function is useful for scenarios where you need a randomized subset of an array while preserving the original array's reference.

functions.name: toKey
functions.summary: The `toKey` function converts a given value into a string key, returning the value as-is if it's already a string or a symbol; otherwise, it coerces the value to a string while handling the special case of negative zero. This function is useful for ensuring consistent key formats when using values in data structures like objects or maps.

functions.name: toSource
functions.summary: The `toSource` function takes a JavaScript function as input and returns its source code as a string. It is useful for debugging or logging purposes, allowing developers to inspect the implementation of a function.

functions.name: updateWrapDetails
functions.summary: The `updateWrapDetails` function modifies an array of wrapper details by adding specific flags based on a provided bitmask, ensuring that each flag is only added once. It is useful for dynamically updating the details of a wrapper based on the active flags, as defined in the `wrapFlags` array.

functions.name: wrapperClone
functions.summary: The `wrapperClone` function creates a clone of a given wrapper object, either by invoking the `clone` method on a `LazyWrapper` instance or by constructing a new `LodashWrapper` with the same properties as the original. This function is useful for preserving the state and behavior of a wrapper object when modifications or transformations are needed without altering the original instance.

functions.name: chunk
functions.summary: The `chunk` function splits an input array into smaller arrays (chunks) of a specified size, returning the final chunk with any remaining elements if the array cannot be evenly divided. This is useful for processing data in manageable segments, such as when displaying items in a paginated format or when handling large datasets.

functions.name: compact
functions.summary: The `compact` function takes an array as input and returns a new array that contains only the truthy values, effectively removing all falsy values such as `false`, `null`, `0`, `""`, `undefined`, and `NaN`. This is useful for filtering out unwanted values from an array, ensuring that only meaningful data remains.

functions.name: concat
functions.summary: The `concat` function creates a new array by concatenating a given array with any additional arrays or values provided as arguments. This is useful for combining multiple data sources into a single array, allowing for flexible data manipulation and organization.

functions.name: drop
functions.summary: The `drop` function creates a new array by removing the first `n` elements from the provided `array`, with a default of 1 element dropped if `n` is not specified. This function is useful for scenarios where you want to skip a certain number of initial elements in an array, such as when processing data or filtering out headers.

functions.name: dropRight
functions.summary: The `dropRight` function creates a new array by removing the last `n` elements from the provided `array`, defaulting to dropping one element if `n` is not specified. This function is useful for scenarios where you need to manipulate arrays by excluding a specific number of elements from the end, such as when processing data or preparing arrays for further operations.

functions.name: dropRightWhile
functions.summary: The `dropRightWhile` function creates a new array by removing elements from the end of the provided `array` until the specified `predicate` function returns a falsy value. This is useful for filtering out trailing elements based on a condition, allowing for more flexible data manipulation.

functions.name: dropWhile
functions.summary: The `dropWhile` function creates a new array by excluding elements from the beginning of the input array until the provided predicate function returns a falsey value. This is useful for filtering out leading elements that do not meet certain criteria, allowing users to easily remove unwanted prefixes from an array.

functions.name: fill
functions.summary: The `fill` function modifies a given array by replacing its elements with a specified value from a defined starting index up to, but not including, an ending index. This is useful for initializing or resetting portions of an array with a specific value, such as setting default values or clearing data.

functions.name: findIndex
functions.summary: The `findIndex` function searches through an array and returns the index of the first element for which the provided predicate function returns a truthy value, starting the search from an optional specified index. This is useful for quickly locating the position of an element that meets certain criteria within an array.

functions.name: findLastIndex
functions.summary: The `findLastIndex` function searches for the last index of an element in an array that satisfies a given predicate function, iterating from the end of the array towards the beginning. It is useful for scenarios where you need to identify the position of the last occurrence of an item that meets specific criteria, such as finding the last matching element in a list.

functions.name: flatten
functions.summary: The `flatten` function takes an array as input and reduces its nesting by one level, returning a new array with the elements flattened accordingly. This is useful for simplifying complex, nested arrays into a more manageable structure for easier data manipulation or processing.

functions.name: flattenDeep
functions.summary: The `flattenDeep` function takes a nested array as input and recursively flattens it into a single-level array, removing all levels of nesting. This is useful for simplifying complex data structures into a more manageable format for processing or analysis.

functions.name: flattenDepth
functions.summary: The `flattenDepth` function takes an array and recursively flattens it up to a specified depth, allowing for the reduction of nested arrays into a single-level array based on the given depth.
